newsitem.title: INDIA: World oil demand seen growing 1.8 mln bpd in 1997.
newsitem.headline: World oil demand seen growing 1.8 mln bpd in 1997.

text.p: Global oil demand in 1997 will grow at 1.8 million barrels per day, fuelled by strong economic growth and a slowing in the decline of demand from the former Soviet Union, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said.

"The combination of the slowdown in FSU (former Soviet Union) demand decline and the stronger global economic growth has led to higher oil demand growth," IEA deputy executive director John Ferriter told an international oil and gas conference on Tuesday.
"We expect growth of 1.8 million barrels per day in 1997."

Ferriter said that between 1989 and 1997, sharp production decreases in the former Soviet Union had masked growth in other areas. The North Sea was the largest contributor to growth in the first half of the 1990s, he said, but gains in other non-OPEC, non-FSU areas were accelerating.
During the 10 years to 1996, oil consumption in the former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe had dropped 44 percent, other experts at the conference said.
"Offshore production growth in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, in Latin America and West Africa are becoming more apparent," Ferriter said.
"New fields in the U.K. and Norway continue to more than compensate for declines in older fields, and increased drilling using advanced drilling technologies is stabilising production in the U.S."

OPEC production has also surged, not only due to the re-entry of Iraqi exports under the United Nations oil-for-food programme, but also due to new field developments, primarily by joint ventures with foreign companies in several other OPEC countries, Ferriter said.

"In 1997 we anticipate that growth in global oil demand will be matched by the growth in non-OPEC supply plus non-OPEC NGLs (natural gas liquids). This leaves little room to accommodate a continuation of the upward trend in OPEC production in addition to the return of limited Iraqi crude under the oil-for-food sales plan," Ferriter said.
"There is thus the potential for renewed market weakness."
